papers.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.
papers.summary_zh: 多模态智能体交互历史不断增长，现有记忆系统依赖压缩记忆的语义检索和预定义表示，容易遗漏相关记忆且忽视查询间异构的证据需求。HiVe-Mem通过横向记忆扩展（用文本与视觉锚点构建关系图，从语义种子扩展邻居以恢复互补信息）与纵向证据组合（每条记忆保留摘要、描述、视觉视图、原图、交互历史等多种证据形式，由轻量可训练选择器按查询自适应组合证据子集）交错协同。在三个多模态记忆基准上，该方法在多种基座模型上一致提升任务表现，同时相比最高效的竞争多模态基线减少约90%的token消耗。
papers.summary_en: As multimodal agents accumulate long interaction histories, existing memory systems rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and predefined representations, which can miss relevant memories and ignore heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. HiVe-Mem interleaves horizontal memory expansion (organizing episodes into a relational graph via textual and visual anchors, expanding semantic seeds with neighbors to recover complementary information) with vertical evidence composition (each memory retains summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history, with a lightweight trainable selector composing a query-adaptive evidence subset). Across three multimodal memory benchmarks, it consistently improves task performance across base models while cutting token consumption by about 90% versus the most efficient competing multimodal baseline.
highlights_zh: 图扩展+多形式证据自适应组合
适用于长程多模态交互记忆

papers.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. We study this reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward--context conflicts, where compliant task completion remains feasible while some executable shortcuts earn more reward than every compliant strategy. Encoding these conflicts in task dynamics lets us generate diverse interactive environments at scale and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. In resource and reporting workflows, task optimization increases real productivity through unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9\% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25\% conflict mixture after 128 updates. The same contextual checks supply a simple binary penalty that supports joint capability and compliance gains and partially mitigates acquired violations. Learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms into workflows with evolving evidence and approval requirements. On 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks, resource-trained safety increases safe completion from 53.1\% to 89.1\% relative to task-only training, while both policies achieve full real work. These results connect a verifiable account of reward-driven misalignment with scalable task construction and safety learning that remains useful under changing execution requirements.
papers.summary_zh: 强化学习在提升任务能力时可能强化违反上下文执行要求的行为，论文通过可验证的奖励-上下文冲突研究这种奖励驱动的失配（含奖励黑客）。方法上将这些冲突编码进任务动态，大规模生成交互环境并从执行历史导出合规反馈，同时用简单二元惩罚支持能力与合规联合提升。结果显示少数冲突暴露即可导致广泛捷径习得（25%冲突混合下128次更新后API任务达97.9%可认证违规获利），而学习到的安全可适应扩展授权并跨机制迁移，在32个未见变化证据任务上将安全完成率从53.1%提升至89.1%且保持全真实工作量。
papers.summary_en: Reinforcement learning can improve task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements; this paper studies such reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward-context conflicts. The authors encode these conflicts in task dynamics to generate diverse interactive environments at scale, derive compliance feedback from execution histories, and show that a simple binary penalty supports joint capability and compliance gains. Minority conflict exposure can cause widespread shortcut acquisition (97.9% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25% conflict mixture after 128 updates), while learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms, raising safe completion from 53.1% to 89.1% on 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks with full real work preserved.
highlights_zh: 可验证奖励-上下文冲突建模
安全可迁移但仅部分缓解
highlights_en: Safety transfers but only partially mitigates

papers.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
papers.abstract: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. However, should AI forecasting systems be adopted, human builders will shoulder the work of building and evaluating them. In this paper, we explore what this work looks like with a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots, sampled from among successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition. Our analysis surfaces the challenges around (1) tuning a bot to acquire factual research, (2) implementing coherent reasoning, and (3) understanding how well one's bot actually does. During their work, builders frequently introduced complexity that did not pay off, and tested in ways that were opportunistic and piecemeal. Our detailed account of their challenges helps clarify what problems should be targeted in upcoming innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.
papers.summary_zh: AI模型推理能力增强使其成为预测工具，但人类构建者需承担构建与评估AI预测系统的工作。本文通过对15名AI预测竞赛成功参与者进行定性访谈，分析了构建预测机器人的实际过程。研究发现构建者面临事实研究调优、连贯推理实现和效果评估三大挑战，且常引入无效复杂性、采用机会主义和零散测试方式，为未来预测工具与人机协作创新指明方向。
papers.summary_en: AI models' growing reasoning capacity makes them attractive for forecasting, yet human builders must shoulder the work of building and evaluating these systems. This paper presents a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots sampled from successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition, analyzing their actual construction work. The analysis surfaces challenges in tuning bots for factual research, implementing coherent reasoning, and assessing bot performance, revealing that builders frequently introduced unproductive complexity and tested opportunistically and piecemeal, clarifying target problems for future innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.
highlights_zh: 揭示预测机器人构建的三大核心挑战
发现构建者常引入无效复杂性且测试零散
为预测领域人机协作工具创新指明方向

papers.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.
papers.summary_zh: AI系统需在有限内存中维护无限交互历史，但稀疏延迟奖励导致标准强化学习难以优化记忆表示及其更新。MaxIM将增量摘要建模为容量受限的信息论奖励塑形问题，通过最大化未来任务相关目标的预测对数似然（预测充分性的变分下界）并引入递归一致性条件，配合参数化非对称评论家提供稠密变分互信息奖励。在长程科学阅读和多轮对话基准上，MaxIM在严格token预算和更长时程下优于RL、监督微调和提示类基线，且无需昂贵的人类偏好标签。
papers.summary_en: AI systems must maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories, but sparse and delayed rewards create severe credit assignment bottlenecks that hinder standard RL from optimizing memory representations and their updates. MaxIM formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem, maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future task-relevant targets (a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency) with a recursive consistency condition, and uses a parameterized asymmetric critic to compute step-wise variational mutual information bounds for dense rewards. On long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks, MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, autorater metrics, and downstream utility under strict token budgets and extended horizons, without expensive human preference labels.
highlights_zh: 信息论奖励塑形+递归一致性
长程任务全面超越RL与SFT基线
无需人类偏好标签，可扩展
highlights_en: Information-theoretic reward shaping with recursive consistency
Outperforms RL and SFT baselines on long-horizon tasks
No human preference labels needed; scalable
